foil.title: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption state
foil.scenario_short: Energy repricing risk from Red Sea maritime disruption will remain elevated at 67% probability over 30 days, driven by 63% energy supply shock pressure and 75% state confirmation, with 4 urgent critical signals...
foil.perspective_strategic: The 63% energy supply shock pressure and 75% state confirmation indicate a strong transmission path through energy supply shock, but the lack of directly matched reporting on Red Sea limits confidence, making the 67% baseline vulnerable to either new headlines or market stabilization.
foil.perspective_contrarian: The 75% confidence level still leaves room for reversal, and the absence of directly matched reporting on Red Sea means the system could drift toward stabilization if no new hard signals emerge, pulling the forecast below 67% to 59%.
foil.actor_lens: Commodity traders: Price whether stress in Red Sea becomes durable over the 30d. Rebalance positions if the probability path moves away from 67%.
foil.top_signal: Red Sea maritime disruption state is feeding energy repricing through energy supply shock, with 63% pressure and 75% state confirmation

seismic-infrastructure.absence_reason: No product publishes a seismic forecast — earthquakes are not predictable, so there is no forecast/intel alternative to azimuth's observed USGS record. This is the honest inverse: for an observed natural-hazard fact, the sourced record IS the only trustworthy source.
